changes: A project cloned from git without Engine/ gets Install engine: the launcher puts in the version Project.json names, without a trial or a list of breaking changes.
When Project.json names another version than the project's engine copy (a teammate moved the project), the project list offers to use that version.
Changing a project's engine writes the version into Project.json; opening an older project writes it too.
The Engines tab shows only the selected version's own release notes, not every version before it.
Engine versions show with their name, like 0.11.1 Cats; versions before names show as Pre-Release.
The Engines tab shows the release notes of versions not downloaded yet.
A New engine version! strip under the top bar tells what a new engine brings in one sentence.
New Project explains an invalid name while you type.
Update checks no longer fail on shared networks: the launcher reads its updates from release downloads instead of the rate-limited GitHub API.
A failed check shows what went wrong.
A new version opens the update panel once at startup.
New engine versions no longer need a launcher update: the New Project list offers the newest one online.
